payload.comparison_population: patients without HCC (controls matched for sex, Child-Pugh grade and platelet count)
payload.supporting_quote: There were no significant differences in the serum total and HMW adiponectin levels between cases and controls.

APRI varied significantly in our cohort (range, 0.16-10.00). Elevated APRI was associated with increased severity of liver disease and 3-month mortality in hospitalized patients with HBV-related cirrhosis.
Our study shows that Tpo, IL-6, and TNFα significantly increased in patients with HCV-ITP compared to the normal population (Tpo:122.577 vs. 40.602; IL-6: 2.175 vs. 0.943; TNFα: 2.460 vs. 1.322).

IL-1α had the highest mean concentration in the HCC group and then in the group of CHC with cirrhosis compared to the group of CHC without cirrhosis. Also, it was higher in all studied groups than in the control group
The baseline factors associated with serious adverse events included liver fibrosis (p = 0.045) and a low platelet count (p = 0.021).
Platelet count increased significantly after splenectomy.
PCs increased significantly from 101.5 ± 68.5 × 10(9) /L before OLT to 162.4 ± 86 × 10(9) /L 1 month after OLT and remained stable for 1 year after the operation.
